config.title: Serialize & Deserialize Binary Tree

intro.title: Serialize & Deserialize Binary Tree
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a program that can convert a binary tree into a string (serialize) and reconstruct the original tree from that string (deserialize). You will learn the core concept of tree traversal, specifically using depth-first search (DFS) to process each node. The main technologies involved are JavaScript functions, recursion, and string manipulation. By the end, you will understand how to preserve and restore the structure of a binary tree using a simple text format.
intro.usecase: Serializing and deserializing binary trees is essential for efficiently storing and transmitting hierarchical data structures in real applications. This pattern appears in web applications that need to save and restore complex UI component trees, such as dashboard layouts with nested panels, collapsible menus with submenus, or form builders with conditional sections. Developers use these techniques when implementing features like saving/loading workspace configurations, syncing application state across devices, or caching complex data structures for performance optimization. In database systems, tree serialization enables efficient storage of hierarchical data like organizational charts, file system directories, or product category trees.

objectives: Construct a binary tree node class with value, left, and right properties
Implement a serialize function that converts a binary tree to a string representation
Apply a deserialize function that reconstructs a binary tree from its string representation
Manipulate tree traversal algorithms to generate and parse serialized data
Initialize test cases to validate serialization and deserialization functionality
Integrate error handling for edge cases like empty trees and invalid input
Configure a complete workflow that serializes and deserializes binary trees end-to-end

content.body: Imagine you need to save a binary tree to a file or send it over a network. How can you represent its structure as a simple string? In this lesson, you'll learn how to serialize and deserialize a binary tree—converting it to and from a string format while preserving its shape.
content.title: Introduction

content.body:
By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
1. Explain why serialization is needed for tree data structures.
2. Apply a traversal order to convert a tree into a string.
3. Implement both serialize and deserialize functions in JavaScript.
4. Handle empty nodes (null values) during the conversion process.
5. Reconstruct the original tree structure from the serialized string.
content.title: What you'll learn

content.body: Look at this simple binary tree with root value 1, left child 2, and right child 3. If you had to write it down as text to share with someone, how would you represent it? Think about what information you need to capture: values, structure, and empty spots.
content.title: Explore the tree
content.visualMetaphor: Show exploring from the root down branches; one level or one branch at a time.

content.body: You likely thought about listing values in some order and marking where branches end. This is the core challenge of serialization: capturing both values and structure in a linear format.
content.title: What you considered

content.body: With larger trees, simply listing values isn't enough—you need to preserve which node is whose child, and where branches are missing. Without a systematic approach, reconstructing the tree becomes impossible.
content.title: Why it gets complex

content.body: We can use tree traversal to explore branches from the root. By visiting nodes in a consistent order (like pre-order: root, left, right) and recording values—including null for empty branches—we create a complete blueprint. To deserialize, we replay the same traversal to rebuild the tree.
content.title: Key idea
content.visualMetaphor: Use branch/root visual reasoning; visiting nodes or exploring levels one at a time.

content.body: We'll use depth-first pre-order traversal for both operations. During serialization, we visit each node, write its value, then recursively explore left and right branches—writing 'null' for empty ones. For deserialization, we read values in the same order, creating nodes and recursively building left and right subtrees.
content.title: The approach

content.body:
1. Serialize: Perform pre-order traversal, appending node values (or 'null') to an array, then join into a string.
2. Deserialize: Split the string back into an array, then recursively consume values to reconstruct nodes and their children.
3. Base case: When we encounter 'null', return null (empty branch).

content.body: Congratulations! You've implemented tree serialization and deserialize using pre-order traversal. Remember: serialization records values and null markers in a specific order; deserialize replays that order to rebuild the tree. This pattern works because tree traversal creates a deterministic blueprint of the structure.
